name: GlassDrawingCanvas
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell plus redundant glass-backdrop-blur-md and border classes stacked on top (lines 457-463, 602-611). The canvas itself has a hard-coded bg-white class (line 639), so the drawing surface is an opaque white box inside the glass and backgroundColor is mostly ignored visually. Grid strokeStyle uses color-mix(var(--glass-white)) (line 161) and the default pen color is var(--glass-black) (line 84). Canvas 2D cannot resolve CSS variables, so both fall back to the default black or are ignored.
motion: Motion fadeIn, gated on isMotionSafe && respectMotionPreference (line 617). useReducedMotion is imported but never used (line 17). Sound effects via useGlassSound on every stroke, undo, and clear.
a11y: Tool buttons have aria-labels, but their 'icons' are single letters such as 'P' or 'B' (line 484). Undo, Redo, Clear, and Export rely on title only and render unicode or emoji (↶ ↷ 🗑 💾, lines 572-594), so they have no accessible name beyond title. The canvas has no role, label, or keyboard alternative. focus:ring-primary/50 is a non-prefixed class.
api: forwardRef, className passthrough. tool is an initial-only value: it seeds state and is never re-synced. data is uncontrolled after mount. The pressureSensitive prop is unused.
ssr: 'use client'. Canvas and Image access happen only in effects. No heavy imports.
fake_complexity: Partly fake. The line, rectangle, circle, and text tool types are offered but every tool draws freehand polylines; there is no shape logic (drawStroke lines 205-256). pressureSensitive is a no-op. Export 'svg' calls canvas.toDataURL('image/svg'), which returns a PNG (line 445). The eraser uses destination-out, which also erases the background colour or image.
duplicates: none direct; overlaps the canvas/trail logic in GlassGestureZone
justification: Not exported from the root, so it is not part of the public API. Half of its advertised tools are fake (shape and text tools just draw freehand). Toolbar icons are letters and emoji. The canvas is a fixed-pixel (800x600) opaque white rectangle that breaks mobile layouts, and the SVG export is mislabelled. Making it real (shape tools, vector export, a responsive DPR-aware canvas, keyboard access) is a product in itself and out of scope for a glass design system. Keep it as an internal demo or remove it.

name: GlassFacetSearch
material_impl: Outer shell is a bespoke elevation map of utility classes (glass-backdrop-blur-md glass-surface-dark/30 border white/12, lines 245-250) rather than the shared primitive. Only the suggestions dropdown uses OptimizedGlass. A hard-coded inline color rgba(255,255,255,0.95) on facet labels (line 552) makes the text invisible on light themes.
motion: framer-motion AnimatePresence. Reduced-motion handling is broken: initial={{opacity:0}} combined with animate={prefersReducedMotion ? {} : {...}} (lines 314-315, 376-377, 435, 452, 567) leaves any element mounted while reduced motion is active stuck at opacity 0 or height 0. Facet panels, suggestions, and results become invisible for exactly the users who asked for less motion. useReducedMotion starts false and flips after mount (src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts:15), so elements mounted later are affected.
a11y: role=search on the root. The suggestions list is not a combobox or listbox: there is no aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, or arrow-key navigation. Result rows are clickable motion.divs with no role, tabIndex, or key handler (lines 449-460), so results cannot be selected by keyboard. The 'select' facet type renders checkboxes for a single choice (lines 643-659) where radio buttons are needed. The clear button has no type and default text sizing.
api: forwardRef, className and ...props passthrough. Mostly controlled (query, facetValues). The variant, size, and elevation naming is local and not shared with the system. handleFacetChange fires an un-cancelled setTimeout(300) per change (line 209), so rapid changes trigger N stale onSearch calls. It also has no unmount cleanup. Index keys are used for suggestions.
ssr: 'use client'. framer-motion is imported. No window access at module scope.
fake_complexity: No AI claims. The debounce is fake (a setTimeout without clearTimeout).
duplicates: GlassFilterPanel (same checkbox/slider/daterange facet renderer, near copy-paste)
justification: This duplicates GlassFilterPanel's facet rendering almost line for line, and other parts of the library already provide search. The reduced-motion pattern hides content, results are mouse-only, the debounce leaks timers, and single-select facets use checkboxes. Rebuild it as a composition: a proper ARIA combobox search field, a shared facet engine for filters, and a results list. It should not remain a standalone 675-line monolith.

name: GlassFileExplorer
material_impl: Triple-defined material. The elevation class map (lines 400-405) is then overridden by inline linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0.05)...), border rgba(255,255,255,0.14), and box-shadow literals (lines 419-430), so the elevation prop has no visual effect. Rows use OptimizedGlass level1 interactive. Selection uses glass-ring-blue-400 and ring-blue-400/40 together (lines 601-617), mixing prefixed and unprefixed classes.
motion: framer-motion. Same broken reduced-motion pattern (initial opacity 0, animate {} at lines 594-597): after navigating folders with reduced motion on, newly mounted rows stay invisible.
a11y: role=region with a label. Rows are OptimizedGlass divs with onClick only: no role=grid/row/option, no tabIndex, no keyboard selection or open. The per-row 'More options' button is opacity-0 until hover (line 727), so keyboard users can't see it, and it only performs 'open' rather than showing a menu. The create-folder 'dialog' is a fixed div with no role=dialog, focus trap, or Escape handling (lines 746-782).
api: forwardRef, style merged. Selection, viewMode, and search are controlled. onFileCopy is declared but never called. The download action is an empty case (line 248). Delete is only reachable through code paths no UI calls: handleContextMenuAction is only ever invoked with 'open'.
ssr: 'use client'. document.createElement runs only in the drag handler.
fake_complexity: Rename and delete UI is unreachable: no UI path calls handleContextMenuAction('rename'/'delete'). The context menu is a stub that comments 'could be expanded to show a menu' (line 730).
duplicates: GlassFileTree (same icon map, formatFileSize, drag ghost, create dialog copy-pasted)
justification: The concept is valid for an app-grade glass system, but the implementation is a facade. The context menu is a stub, rename and delete can't be reached, the rows have no keyboard model, and the dialog is not a dialog. The material is defined three times with inline rgba overriding the elevation API. Rebuild it on a shared FileItem model with the library's Menu, Dialog, and roving-tabindex grid, and share the icon and size utilities with GlassFileTree.

name: GlassFileTree
material_impl: Bespoke utility-class elevation map (lines 385-390). No shared primitive: the create dialog is hand-rolled glass-surface-subtle/5 with a ring.
motion: framer-motion height/opacity expand using the same broken reduced-motion pattern (lines 520-525): with reduced motion on, expanded children mount at height 0 and opacity 0 and are never shown, so the tree cannot be expanded at all for those users.
a11y: No role=tree/treeitem/group, no aria-expanded, no aria-level, and no arrow-key navigation. The expand chevron GlassButton has no aria-label and is 16x16 px (line 429) even though it carries the glass-touch-target class. The context-menu button has no label and an empty onClick (lines 504-514). Rows are clickable divs.
api: forwardRef, but GlassFileTreeProps does not extend HTMLAttributes, yet ...props is spread. The virtualize prop is unused. allowRename, allowCopy, and allowMove are dead: handleContextMenuAction is never called, so rename and create can't be reached. The copy and move branches are empty comments (lines 169-178).
fake_complexity: 'virtualize', rename, create, copy, and move are advertised but unimplemented or unreachable. TreeNodeComponent is declared inside render (line 392), so every parent render remounts the whole subtree: state is lost, the rename input loses focus, and drag state breaks.
target: GlassTreeView (single WAI-ARIA tree with file-icon renderer preset)
justification: This is the third tree implementation in the library. It is inaccessible (no tree roles or arrow keys) and has an architectural bug: a component defined in render, which remounts the subtree on every render. Several allow* flags do nothing, and expansion is invisible under reduced motion. Fold its file-icon and size display into a single accessible GlassTreeView as a renderer preset, then delete this file.

name: GlassFileUpload
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (frosted, level1/2) for the dropzone and file rows. This is the correct primitive, but state colours are utility classes (glass-surface-blue/20, glass-border-red), and destructive tokens border-destructive/50 and bg-destructive/5 are unprefixed classes that likely don't exist (line 519). Icons are inline SVG paths instead of the icon set, and action icons are text glyphs ('↑', '👁', '×').
motion: Motion preset slideDown per file. useReducedMotion is imported but unused (line 19), so reduced-motion behaviour depends on the Motion primitive internals.
a11y: The dropzone is role=button with tabIndex, but there is no onKeyDown, so Enter and Space do nothing for keyboard users (lines 653-685). Errors are not announced (no aria-live). maxFiles overflow silently returns with no feedback (lines 292-294).
api: forwardRef with a reasonable controlled/uncontrolled split (files/defaultFiles). Overlapping props: variant='compact' vs compact, and variant='minimal' implies compact. showPreviews is effectively dead because file.preview is never generated (no URL.createObjectURL).
fake_complexity: Upload progress is simulated: setInterval adds +10% up to 90% regardless of real transfer (lines 340-353), and it mutates objects in place. In controlled mode the progress writes go to internalFiles, which is never displayed. 'Upload All' calls handleUpload for each file with a stale visibleFiles closure, so concurrent commits overwrite each other and only the last file reaches 'completed' (lines 751-755). Math.random IDs.
duplicates: src/components/input/GlassFileUpload.tsx (518 lines, separate component with the same name and its own screenshot)
justification: File upload is a core component every product needs, and this one uses the right primitive. But two components share the same name, the progress bar is fake, batch upload has a race condition, and the dropzone can't be operated from the keyboard. Merge both into one Dropzone with real progress callbacks (onUpload(file, {onProgress})), object-URL previews, aria-live errors, and key handling. It can then be a solid KEEP-tier component.

name: GlassFilterBar
material_impl: Plain utility classes (glass-bg-white/8, border white/10). Translucent fill only, with no blur, no primitive, and no shadow or specular edge, so it is a flat translucent strip.
a11y: role=region with aria-label, an aria-hidden icon, and remove buttons labelled per filter. The remove 'x' button is a literal lowercase x with px-1 padding, giving a roughly 16 px target that fails the 24/44 px target guidance. It has no focus-visible class.
api: forwardRef, HTMLAttributes passthrough, a small and clean prop surface. Its filter chips should reuse the library's GlassChip/Tag rather than ad-hoc spans.
fake_complexity: None. It does what it says.
justification: This is the most honest component in the shard: small, typed, forwardRef, with no fake features. It needs to compose the system's chip/tag component (with a proper dismiss icon and 24 px+ targets), adopt the shared glass surface primitive instead of a flat bg-white/8, and gain a test and a visual certification target. Positioned as the 'active filters' row that pairs with GlassFilterPanel.

name: GlassFilterPanel
material_impl: Contradictory material. The class map applies glass-surface-dark/50 for every elevation (lines 223-228), then an inline style overrides the background with rgba(255,255,255,0.26/0.28/0.32) (lines 246-251). The result is a white-ish panel whose 'dark' classes are dead. Hard-coded maxWidth 28rem.
motion: Correct reduced-motion pattern here (initial={prefersReducedMotion ? false : {opacity:0}}, lines 380, 416). This is the only file in the shard that does it right, which shows the bug elsewhere is copy-paste drift.
a11y: Group toggles are buttons, but they have no aria-expanded or aria-controls and no type. The preset 'dialog' is a fixed div with no role, focus trap, or Escape handling (lines 441-472). Apply is disabled unless filters are active, which blocks applying an intentionally empty state. The 'required' marker is a bare '*' with no text alternative.
api: forwardRef, but its props don't extend HTMLAttributes while ...props is spread. Controlled values/onChange. contained and compact silently drop all groups except the first (line 204, slice(0,1)) and truncate options to 3 (line 509). This is a surprising data-loss behaviour, built to make screenshots fit.
fake_complexity: Compact mode hides real filter groups for presentation. The '+N more' text is not interactive.
target: canonical facet/filter engine absorbing GlassFacetSearch facets
justification: This is the better of the two facet implementations and should become the canonical one. It needs a single material source (drop the inline rgba overrides), proper disclosure semantics, the library Dialog for presets, and removal of the compact-mode group truncation, which exists only to make screenshots fit. Paired with GlassFilterBar it forms a coherent filtering family.

name: GlassFocusRing
material_impl: CSS module (GlassFocusRing.module.css) with a ::before ring using CSS vars and blur. The ring has z-index:-1, so it renders behind any parent with a background or stacking context and can be invisible on glass cards.
motion: CSS opacity transition driven by --glass-focus-duration. There is no prefers-reduced-motion rule, but the change is minor (opacity only).
a11y: Harmful pattern. The wrapper div gets tabIndex=0 (line 73) around an already focusable child, creating a double tab stop with an unlabelled, roleless focusable div. useGlassFocus attaches 'focus' (not focusin) and treats relatedTarget as meaning keyboard, which is an unreliable heuristic (src/hooks/extended/useGlassFocus.ts handleFocus). When multiple children are passed they are wrapped in an aria-hidden span (line 32), hiding the focusable content from assistive tech.
api: Not forwardRef. GlassFocusRingProps advertises target, width, ringStyle (solid/dashed/dotted/glow), and shape, none of which are used (component lines 16-26 versus src/components/interactive/types.ts:386-411). It is not a Slot/asChild, which this kind of component needs.
fake_complexity: ringStyle and shape are fake props. The 'animated' claim amounts to an opacity fade.
target: token-driven :focus-visible ring in the base glass styles + optional asChild FocusRing Slot
justification: A focus-ring wrapper that adds an extra tab stop and can hide its children from assistive technology makes accessibility worse. Three focus-indicator components exist. The premium answer is one token-driven :focus-visible ring baked into every interactive primitive (outline plus specular halo that works on glass), optionally exposed as an asChild Slot. Replace this component and its siblings with that.

name: GlassFormBuilder
material_impl: Composes GlassCard per section and the library inputs, which is the right approach. Several layout classes are unprefixed Tailwind ('flex items-center justify-between', 'font-semibold text-foreground', 'cursor-pointer', 'w-full', lines 536, 544, 593). There is no Tailwind config in the repo, and these classes only partly exist in storybook-utility-shim.css (shipped through src/styles/index.css:25), so layout depends on a Storybook shim.
motion: Motion slideDown per section, with no explicit reduced-motion handling.
a11y: Inputs are labelled through library components. The radio group uses a <label> as a group title instead of fieldset/legend (lines 443-451). The collapsible section header is a clickable div with a nested GlassButton that has no onClick (it relies on bubbling, lines 591-633). The submit has a redundant aria-label. Errors are not linked to an error summary on submit.
api: forwardRef<HTMLForm>, but the props don't extend form attributes while ...props is spread. values and errors seed state only and never re-sync (lines 208-209), so it is not truly controlled. autoSave calls onSubmit (line 258), conflating autosave with submit. The 'file' field type is declared but renders null (lines 28, 476). The pattern string is compiled into a RegExp on every validation.
fake_complexity: The conditional logic and validation are real but minimal. The 'wizard' variant only changes the gap size; there are no steps.
target: GlassForm + GlassFormField (schema renderer as a thin helper)
justification: This is one of at least seven form or wizard implementations. The 'wizard' variant is fake, the file type renders nothing, the controlled API is broken, autosave triggers submit, and layout depends on a Storybook utility shim. Keep at most a thin schema-to-GlassFormField renderer layered on the canonical GlassForm, then remove the rest.

name: GlassGallery
material_impl: GlassCard variant=elevated per tile with glass-sheen and glass-tilt. The lightbox is a glass-surface-dark/90 div. The aspect-ratio and grid-column classes are unprefixed Tailwind ('aspect-square', 'aspect-[3/4]', 'grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-${n}', lines 132-147). These classes do not exist in the shipped CSS (only .glass-aspect-square and .glass-grid-cols-2 exist in src/styles/glass.css:3782, 3965), and the template-literal column classes could never be generated. The responsive grid and aspect ratios don't work: tiles fall back to .grid with no template (one column) in the shim.
motion: CSS glass-animate-fade-in and slide-in-up with staggered delays. There is no reduced-motion gating at the component level. The image scale on hover uses a non-existent group-hover class.
a11y: A transparent overlay button carries the image label (good). The lightbox has no role=dialog, aria-modal, focus trap, or Escape handler of its own; it relies on GlassImageViewer's global window listener. Like and Share buttons are no-ops (lines 342-358) with misleading labels. The list layout stacks an empty full-size button above the image (lines 386-400), which breaks the layout.
api: Not forwardRef, and the props don't extend HTMLAttributes while ...props is spread. The layout prop ('masonry') is ignored, because view mode is internal state initialised to 'grid' (line 124). The lightbox index comes from the filtered list but indexes the unfiltered images[] (lines 211, 494), so filtering opens the wrong image. The lightbox stacks its own prev/next buttons over GlassImageViewer's, so there are two sets of navigation.
fake_complexity: Masonry is advertised but not implemented. Like and Share are fake.
justification: A glass media gallery could be a showcase, but this one has dead responsive and aspect classes, so the 'grid' isn't really a grid. Masonry is fake, Like and Share do nothing, the lightbox opens the wrong image after filtering and shows duplicate navigation, and the list layout is broken. Rebuild it on prefixed tokens and CSS grid with a real Dialog-based lightbox, composing GlassLazyImage tiles. ImageList should either merge in or be removed.

name: GlassGestureZone
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shells with redundant blur and border classes. The canvas uses hard-coded #FF6B6B and #4ADE80 and 'white' (lines 649, 663, 684). trailColor defaults to 'hsl(var(--glass-color-primary))' (line 113), which Canvas 2D cannot parse, so the trail falls back to black. Unprefixed bg-green-500/20 and text-red-400 classes.
motion: A permanent requestAnimationFrame loop redraws the canvas every frame even when idle (lines 716-729). Two setInterval(16 ms) loops call setState with freshly mapped arrays forever (lines 567-600), so the component re-renders around 120 times a second while idle, even with empty arrays. The trail is hidden under reduced motion, but the loops keep running.
a11y: The controls look interactive but are dead. The 'Active' button has onClick={() => {}}, and the sensitivity slider and all three checkboxes have onChange={() => {}} (lines 765-832), so they are controlled inputs that cannot change. The canvas has no keyboard alternative. A hard-coded id 'gesture-sensitivity' collides across instances.
api: forwardRef. aria-label and data-testid are read from props and then also spread. maxGestureDuration, recognitionTimeout, and maxTouches are unused.
fake_complexity: The 'Gesture recognition' uses naive DTW against hard-coded templates. 'tap' and 'double_tap' are identical single-point templates, so double-tap can never be distinguished. 'pinch' is a three-point horizontal line, not a two-pointer pinch. Its 10 stories make a dead-control demo look feature-rich.
justification: Not exported publicly. Its controls are dead, its gesture recognition is cosmetic (tap and double-tap are the same template, and 'pinch' is a line), and it burns CPU with an always-on rAF loop plus two 60 Hz setState intervals. Fixed pixel sizes break mobile. It duplicates MultiDimensionalGestureRecognizer. Nothing here belongs in a premium design system. If gesture support is needed, expose a headless usePointerGesture hook built on the existing gesturePhysics.

name: GlassGradientPicker
material_impl: GlassCard plus ContrastGuard wrappers around nearly every heading (ContrastGuard overuse). Stop rows use unprefixed 'flex items-center border-primary bg-primary/20 border-white/20 bg-white/5' (lines 467-470). The default stops are near-white rgba (lines 112-115), so the out-of-box preview is a barely visible white-on-white swatch, consistent with the low-contrast certification capture.
motion: Motion fadeIn. useReducedMotion is imported but unused (line 18).
a11y: Range and colour inputs have aria-labels, and presets are role=button with key handling (good). Stop rows are clickable divs. The icons are semantically wrong: the Upload icon means 'Add stop' and the Download icon means 'Remove stop' (lines 456, 513).
api: Not forwardRef. The value prop is ignored, so it cannot be controlled. onChange never fires for manual angle, type, or stop edits; only presets and random do. On those paths it receives a stale gradient string, because generateGradient reads the previous state (lines 232-233, 255-256). stops.sort() mutates React state in place (line 171). Index keys are used for stops.
ssr: 'use client'. navigator.clipboard is used only in a handler.
fake_complexity: Preset swatches build invalid CSS for radial and conic types ('radial-gradient(0deg, ...)', line 561), so the Mist and Graphite presets render transparent. The random colour generator can produce fewer than 6 hex digits (line 242). Reset restores different colours (#7CD3FF/#A78BFA) than the initial state.
justification: A gradient picker is useful for theme tooling, but this one cannot be controlled, doesn't emit changes for most edits, emits stale values otherwise, renders broken preset swatches, and uses inverted icon semantics. Rebuild it on GlassColorPicker with a draggable stop track, a controlled value of {type, angle, stops}, and a deterministic CSS serializer, or drop it from the core package.

name: GlassImageViewer
material_impl: GlassCard shell with glass-surface-dark/50 blur overlays for the info and dots bars. Many layout classes are unprefixed and missing from the shipped CSS ('aspect-video', 'object-contain', 'bg-black/20', 'h-screen', 'fixed inset-0 z-50 rounded-none', lines 439-513), so the stage has no intrinsic aspect ratio and objectFit does nothing. The dots bar uses 'glass--left-1-2' (line 705), a typo for left-1/2, so it is mispositioned.
motion: The autoplay correctly stops under reduced motion (line 391) and the spinner is gated (line 483). The transform transition class is unprefixed.
a11y: Controls are labelled GlassButtons (good). The keyboard handler is a global window keydown (lines 302-357): arrows, +, -, 0, and R are hijacked page-wide, including while the user types in inputs elsewhere, and multiple viewers or the Gallery lightbox respond simultaneously. The fullscreen mode is not the Fullscreen API and has no focus trap. Dot buttons are 8 px. Pan is mouse-only, with no touch or pointer support.
api: Not forwardRef, and the props don't extend HTMLAttributes while ...props is spread. initialIndex is not re-synced. The wheel handler calls preventDefault on React's passive wheel listener (line 294), which is ineffective and logs a warning, so the page scrolls while zooming. During autoplay the index changes without calling onImageChange or resetting imageLoading.
ssr: 'use client'. window and document are accessed only in effects and handlers.
fake_complexity: Mostly real (zoom, rotate, pan, slideshow), but the pan maths applies translate after scale and rotate, so dragging moves in rotated or scaled space.
justification: The feature set is real and close to useful. The main blockers are fixable: the page-wide keyboard hijack (scope it to a focused container), dead unprefixed layout classes, the left-1/2 typo, the passive-wheel preventDefault, pointer events for touch pan and pinch, and Dialog-based fullscreen. After that it should become the single lightbox engine for GlassGallery.

name: GlassInfiniteScroll
material_impl: Mostly structural. The loading pill is glass-surface-subtle/10 plus blur. The container uses unprefixed 'overflow-y-auto' and 'flex flex-col-reverse' (lines 226-227), which depend on the shim.
motion: Motion fadeIn for the indicators. useReducedMotion is imported but unused (line 12). The spinner is not gated.
a11y: No aria-busy, no role=feed, and no aria-live for 'Loading more…' or the end-of-list message. The retry button is labelled with text (fine).
api: Not forwardRef, and the props don't extend HTMLAttributes while ...props is spread. The observer root is the component itself, so it only works if the consumer supplies a height. A page-scroll mode is missing. The loading and error props are mirrored into internal state, which is half-controlled and can desync. In reverse mode the sentinel ref swaps between two DOM nodes, and the observer effect may not re-run.
ssr: 'use client'. IntersectionObserver is used only in an effect.
fake_complexity: None. It is a real IntersectionObserver implementation.
justification: A small, mostly honest utility. Needed changes: forwardRef, a root option (container or viewport), proper feed/aria-busy/aria-live semantics, removal of the mirrored state, prefixed classes, and a fix for the reverse-mode sentinel. It is low risk and worth keeping, but it is plumbing, not a visual showcase.

name: GlassInlineEdit
material_impl: A raw <input> with a transparent background and a white/20 border, not the library's GlassInput, so it is inconsistent with the other text fields. On light backgrounds a border-white/20 line is effectively invisible.
a11y: Uses a real button to enter edit mode and handles Enter and Escape. The input's aria-label is the placeholder ('Edit…') rather than a field name. Focus does not return to the trigger button after save or cancel, because the button remounts and nothing focuses it. role=group is fine.
api: Function component, not forwardRef. Only value, onChange, placeholder, and className are accepted: no label, disabled, validation, onCancel, multiline, or blur-to-save. Uses unprefixed 'inline-flex items-center'.
justification: The behaviour is right and the component is small. It should compose GlassInput, accept a label, disabled, validate, and save-on-blur, use forwardRef, and return focus to the trigger after commit or cancel. It then becomes the shared inline-rename primitive that FileTree and FileExplorer reuse instead of hand-rolling.

name: GlassKanban
material_impl: Columns are unprefixed 'bg-white/5 border border-white/10' (line 483). Cards are OptimizedGlass with unprefixed priority border classes (border-red-400/50 and similar, lines 583-585). The column title has an inline color default of 'white' (line 505), which is invisible on light themes. 'consciousness-*' classes are applied with no evidence that matching CSS exists.
motion: Motion fadeIn. animationDelay is set on cards that have no animation class. useMotionPreferenceContext is imported but unused.
a11y: Cards and columns are clickable divs with no role, tabIndex, or keyboard handling. The Plus and More buttons have no aria-label and no onClick (lines 531-556). There is no drag-and-drop, let alone keyboard DnD.
api: Not forwardRef. Hooks are called conditionally (`predictive ? usePredictiveEngine() : null`, lines 133-138), which violates the Rules of Hooks: toggling a prop at runtime crashes React. enableDragDrop and onCardMove are declared but never used. className is applied twice (lines 390, 402). A window._kanbanSpatialAudio global is used as a cross-instance channel (line 284). Six 'Consciousness' variant wrappers are exported.
ssr: 'use client'. Imports the advanced eye-tracking, biometric, predictive, spatial-audio, and achievement modules even when they are unused, which adds bundle weight. document.querySelectorAll runs in an effect.
fake_complexity: Severe. Eye tracking is explicitly disabled ('Eye tracking functionality temporarily disabled', lines 200-202). Interaction recording passes a mock MouseEvent (lines 302-314). The 'predictive workflow suggestions' come from an engine call. The Kanban has no drag and drop at all, despite the enableDragDrop default of true.
justification: A Kanban without drag and drop, with conditional hooks that crash when props change, disabled 'eye tracking', mock-event 'consciousness' recording, and a window global for audio. It is the textbook fake-complexity component. A second Kanban (GlassKanbanBoard) already exists. Delete this one and its six 'Consciousness' variants, and invest in a single accessible board built on dnd-kit-style keyboard DnD.

name: GlassKeyValueEditor
material_impl: Raw <input>s with a transparent background and a white/20 border, not GlassInput. There is no container surface: rows float with no glass. The remove and add actions are text-only GlassButtons.
a11y: Per-row aria-labels and group roles (good). There is no duplicate-key or empty-key validation messaging. Removing a row shifts focus unpredictably because index keys are used.
api: Function component, not forwardRef, controlled only (value/onChange). Index keys (line 41) cause input state and focus to jump when a middle row is removed. No disabled, readOnly, placeholder, or validation props.
justification: An honest, small, controlled component that is useful in dev-tool and settings UIs. It should compose GlassInput and icon buttons, use stable row IDs, add duplicate-key validation, forwardRef, and a disabled state, and sit on a proper glass surface. That is low effort.

name: GlassLazyImage
material_impl: The info bar uses an inline backgroundColor rgba(255,255,255,0.2) with blur (lines 340-341), which leaves white text on a white tint with no contrast handling. The actions menu uses glass-surface-dark/80. Unprefixed 'relative overflow-hidden group cursor-pointer', 'w-full h-full', 'object-cover', and 'opacity-0/100' classes (lines 264, 300-315) mean the fade and object-fit may be dead outside Storybook.
motion: Nested Motion fadeIn wrappers (three levels). useReducedMotion is imported but unused (line 15). The spinner is not gated.
a11y: The root is a clickable Motion div with no role or keyboard handling but always shows cursor-pointer. The actions trigger ('⋯') has no aria-label or aria-expanded, and the menu has no role=menu, Escape, or outside-click handling (lines 380-436). It is revealed only on hover (opacity-0), so keyboard users can't see it. The placeholder image's alt is 'Loading...', which should be empty.
api: Not forwardRef, and the props don't extend img attributes, so there is no srcSet, sizes, or decoding. It double-lazy-loads: IntersectionObserver plus loading='lazy'. The navigator.clipboard fallback is not awaited and errors are swallowed.
ssr: 'use client'. IntersectionObserver is used in an effect, and there is no fallback when it is unsupported. On the server the image isn't rendered at all (isInView=false), which hurts LCP and SEO.
fake_complexity: The zoom action is a stub: handleZoom says 'Zoom functionality would be implemented here' (lines 195-199). The rest is real.
target: GlassImage (single image primitive: native lazy + blur-up + optional overlay slot)
justification: Blur-up lazy images are a legitimate primitive, but this one bundles a hover-only, unlabelled action menu with a stub zoom, and it never renders the img during SSR. It doesn't pass through img attributes and relies on unprefixed classes. Split it into a lean GlassImage (native loading and srcSet passthrough, blur-up placeholder, an aspect-ratio token) with composable overlays. The actions belong to the gallery or card, not the image.

name: _shard_notes
justification: Screenshot review: the Read tool returned empty results for every PNG and JPEG in this run, so visual scores are based on code plus pixel statistics computed from the certification PNGs. 15 of the 17 captures have a white corner background (255), a mean luminance around 243-247, and a standard deviation of 8-15. That means a near-white page with faint, low-contrast grey content; there is no rich material, depth, or colour. The exceptions are the gallery, image viewer, and lazy image, which show photo content. All 17 targets are marked 'passed' with empty issuesFound in reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification.json, despite the functional defects listed above, so that certification is not evidence of quality. GlassFilterBar has no certification target.
